1.3 "Delivery Point" means the Buyer's central stores at 22 Marina, Lagos Island, unless otherwise notified in writing at least 7 days prior to a scheduled delivery.

1.4 "Force Majeure" shall have the meaning ascribed in Clause 12.

1.7 "Specification" means the quality and grading standards set out in Schedule 2, together with any written amendments agreed by both parties.

2. SUPPLY OF GOODS

2.1 The Supplier shall supply the Goods to the Buyer in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, the Specifications, and any delivery schedule issued under Clause 4.

2.2 The Goods shall be sourced, processed, and packaged in compliance with all applicable Nigerian laws, regulations, and standards, including but not limited to NAFDAC requirements and the Lagos State environmental health regulations.

2.3 The Supplier warrants that the Goods are fit for human consumption, free from defects, and of merchantable quality.

2.4 Title to the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery at the Delivery Point and acceptance by the Buyer's receiving officer.

3. COMMITTED MONTHLY SUPPLY VOLUME

3.1 Under the Supply Agreement 2024-2026, the committed monthly supply volume in tons is 40. Record status: current. This volume represents the aggregate of all Goods categories listed in Schedule 1, measured as delivered weight at the Delivery Point.

3.2 The Buyer shall place monthly orders against this committed volume, and the Supplier shall make available the full 40 tons each month, subject to Clause 3.3.

3.3 The Buyer may, by written notice at least 15 days before the start of a month, reduce its order for that month to not less than 75% of the committed volume. Any such reduction shall not carry forward to subsequent months.

3.5 If the Buyer's actual monthly offtake exceeds the committed volume, the Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to meet the excess, at the prices set out in Schedule 3.

4. DELIVERY SCHEDULES

4.1 The Buyer shall issue a rolling delivery schedule covering each calendar month, specifying the quantities, product mix, and delivery dates. Schedules shall be issued at least 10 working days before the first delivery date in the month.

4.2 Deliveries shall be made on the dates specified, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday, excluding public holidays.

4.3 The Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing at least 48 hours before each delivery, confirming the vehicle registration, driver name, and estimated time of arrival.

4.4 Each delivery shall be accompanied by a delivery note stating the Goods, quantities, batch numbers, and the date of manufacture and expiry where applicable.

4.5 The Buyer shall provide reasonable access, unloading assistance, and storage space at the Delivery Point. Delays caused by the Buyer's failure to provide such facilities shall not constitute a breach by the Supplier, provided the Supplier's vehicle arrives within the agreed delivery window.

4.6 If the Supplier anticipates a delay of more than 4 hours, it shall inform the Buyer's procurement officer immediately and propose a revised delivery time. Repeated delays may be treated as a breach under Clause 11.
5.3.1 The Supplier shall issue an invoice for each delivery, or for multiple deliveries within a single calendar week, at its discretion. Each invoice shall reference the relevant delivery notes, the order number, and the month to which the delivery relates.

5.3.2 Invoices shall be submitted to the Buyer's accounts department by email at accounts@grandpalate.ng, or by such other means as the Buyer may notify in writing.

5.3.3 The Buyer shall pay each undisputed invoice within 30 days of receipt, by bank transfer to the account stated on the invoice. Payment shall be deemed made on the date the funds are credited to the Supplier's account.

5.3.4 If the Buyer disputes any part of an invoice, it shall notify the Supplier in writing within 10 working days of receipt, specifying the disputed items. The undisputed portion shall be paid by the due date, and the parties shall use reasonable endeavours to resolve the dispute within 15 working days.

5.3.5 The Supplier shall include on each invoice the value added tax (VAT) separately, at the prevailing rate, and shall provide a valid tax invoice as required by the Federal Inland Revenue Service.

5.3.6 Late payment of undisputed amounts shall attract interest at the rate of 2% per month, compounded. The Buyer shall reimburse the Supplier for any bank charges incurred as a result of late payment.

5.3.7 The Supplier may suspend further deliveries if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than 45 days after the due date, provided it has given the Buyer at least 7 days' written notice of its intention to suspend.

---

6. QUALITY AND SPECIFICATIONS

6.1 All Goods supplied under this Agreement shall conform to the specifications set out in Schedule 1, and shall be of merchantable quality, fit for the purpose for which they are intended, and comply with all applicable Nigerian food safety regulations, including the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) requirements.

The Supply Agreement 2024-2026 sets the unit price per ton in naira at 450000. Record status: current.

6.2 The Supplier shall maintain a documented quality management system and shall, upon reasonable request, provide the Buyer with certificates of analysis, batch records, and evidence of NAFDAC registration for each product category.

6.3 The Buyer may, at its own cost, arrange for independent testing of samples taken from any delivery. If the testing reveals that the Goods do not conform to the specifications, the Buyer shall notify the Supplier within 5 working days, and the Supplier shall, at its option, either replace the affected Goods or issue a credit note.

6.4 The Supplier shall notify the Buyer immediately in the event of any product recall, food safety alert, or regulatory action affecting the Goods, and shall cooperate fully with the Buyer in managing any consequent withdrawal.

---

7. PACKAGING AND LABELLING

7.1 The Goods shall be packed in food-grade packaging suitable for the mode of transport and storage, and in standard trade quantities as set out in Schedule 1.

7.2 Each package shall be labelled with the product name, batch number, net weight, date of manufacture, best-before or expiry date, and the Supplier's name and address.

7.3 The Buyer may request special packaging or labelling for particular outlets or promotional events, at least 7 days in advance. Any additional cost shall be agreed in writing before the order is placed.

---
8. WARRANTIES

8.1 The Supplier warrants that for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of delivery (the "Warranty Period"), the Goods shall:

(a) conform in all material respects to the specifications set out in Schedule 1;

(b) be free from material defects in design, material, and workmanship;

(c) be of satisfactory quality and fit for any purpose held out by the Supplier or made known to the Supplier in writing;

(d) comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards in force in the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including but not limited to NAFDAC requirements.

8.2 The Supplier further warrants that it has good and marketable title to the Goods, that the Goods are free from all encumbrances, and that the Goods do not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights.

8.3 If any of the Goods do not conform to the warranties set out in Clause 8.1, the Buyer shall notify the Supplier in writing within 10 working days of discovery. Upon receipt of such notice, the Supplier shall, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming Goods at no cost to the Buyer, or issue a credit note in respect of the non-conforming Goods. This remedy shall be in addition to any other rights the Buyer may have under this Agreement or at law.

8.4 The warranties in this Clause 8 shall not apply to the extent that any defect or non-conformance arises from:

(a) misuse, mishandling, or abnormal storage conditions by the Buyer or its agents;

(b) normal wear and tear;

(c) failure to follow the Supplier's written storage or handling instructions;

(d) alterations or repairs carried out by any person other than the Supplier or its authorised representatives.

8.5 THE WARRANTIES SET OUT IN THIS CLAUSE 8 ARE THE ONLY WARRANTIES GIVEN BY THE SUPPLIER IN RESPECT OF THE GOODS AND ARE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, CONDITIONS, TERMS, OR REPRESENTATIONS, WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, STATUTORY OR OTHERWISE, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT THAT SUCH WARRANTIES CANNOT BE EXCLUDED BY LAW.

---

9. LIABILITY AND INDEMNITY

9.1 Nothing in this Agreement shall limit or exclude either party's liability for:

(a) death or personal injury caused by its negligence, or that of its employees, agents, or subcontractors;

(b) fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation;

(c) any other liability that cannot be limited or excluded by applicable law.

9.2 Subject to Clause 9.1, neither party shall be liable to the other, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty, or otherwise, for any indirect or consequential loss or damage, loss of profits, loss of business, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated savings, loss of goodwill, or loss of or corruption to data, arising under or in connection with this Agreement.

Archive item 2: Change Request CR-2024-07
Source format: change request

**3.1 Volume and Schedule**

Current weekly order: 25 tonnes (delivered in two drops: Tuesday and Friday).
Proposed weekly order: 15 tonnes (single drop on Tuesday).

The reduction of 10 tonnes per week will bring the monthly intake from roughly 100 tonnes to 60 tonnes. This aligns with the average monthly sales we have recorded over the last two months (May: 58 tonnes; June: 61 tonnes). We are not requesting a change to the unit pricing or the payment terms in this CR.

**3.2 Delivery Schedule**

There is a risk that if we need to revert to two drops later in the year (e.g., for the December festive season), the Friday slot may no longer be available. We will need to give Lagoon at least four weeks notice for any reversion.

**3.3 Storage and Staffing**

With a single weekly delivery, the receiving team at the Festac store will need to process the full 15 tonnes in one day instead of splitting it across two days. The store manager has confirmed they can handle this with the current crew, but they will need the forklift operator to stay an extra hour on Tuesday. This has been budgeted for in the current staffing plan.

The Lekki store will continue to receive a transfer from Festac rather than a direct delivery. The transfer quantity will be reduced proportionally.

**3.4 Supplier Impact**

Lagoon Cold Chain has been informed verbally of the proposed reduction. Their account manager, Mrs. Adeyemi, noted that the 25-tonne weekly volume was a key factor in their pricing. Reducing to 15 tonnes may trigger a review of the unit price under Clause 8.2 of the framework agreement. We have requested a written quote for the reduced volume scenario; it has not yet been received.

**3.5 Quality Issues**

Change Request CR-2024-07 requested volume reduction in tons 10 tons. Record status: superseded.

The quality complaints from the Ikorodu outlet are being tracked separately under the non-conformance log. This CR does not address those claims. However, the reduced volume will give us time to clear the suspect batch before new stock arrives. We have asked Lagoon to provide the slaughter and packing dates for the last three deliveries.

**4. APPROVAL STATUS**

This change request is **pending approval** as of the date of submission. It has been routed to the following:

- Operations Director (for schedule impact)
- Head of Culinary (for menu impact)
- Finance Controller (for cost review)

Approvals are expected by 10 July 2024. If approved, the new volume will take effect from the delivery of 16 July 2024.

**5. PROPOSED CHANGE REQUEST CR-2024-07 REQUESTED VOLUME REDUCTION IN TONS 10 TONS.**

This is the controlling statement of the requested change. The contract annex will be amended accordingly once all approvals are received. The current 25-tonne weekly volume remains in force until the amendment is executed.

**6. ATTACHMENTS**

- Attachment A: Inventory report for Festac and Lekki cold rooms (30 June 2024)
- Attachment B: Sales data by outlet, May–June 2024
- Attachment C: Draft amendment to Annex B of AFR/SUP/2023-118

**7. NOTES**

- The maintenance log for the Festac compressor is attached for reference.
- The supplier has a 48-hour response window under the framework agreement; we expect their formal response by Monday.
- If the volume reduction is not approved, we will need to explore alternative storage at a third-party facility, which will incur additional cost.

**9. EFFECTIVE DATE AND IMPLEMENTATION**

The approved volume reduction takes effect from the delivery scheduled for **16 July 2024**. This is consistent with the timeline proposed in Section 4 of the original submission. The supplier has been notified by email and has confirmed receipt of the amendment notice. Their written acknowledgment is attached to the contract file.

The following operational adjustments will be implemented from the effective date:

- Weekly order volume for Lagoon Poultry will be set at 17 tonnes (25 tonnes original minus 8 tonnes reduction). This is the net ordering quantity to be used by the procurement team until further notice.
- The Festac cold room will be cleared of existing stock before the first reduced-volume delivery. The maintenance log for the compressor is referenced in Section 7; the unit is currently operating within acceptable parameters.
- The Lekki outlet will receive its normal allocation. The Ikorodu outlet's quality complaints are noted but remain outside the scope of this CR and are being tracked under the non-conformance log.

Clause 8.2 of the framework agreement provides for a unit price review in the event of a volume change exceeding 10 percent of the original commitment. The approved reduction of 8 tonnes from the 25-tonne baseline is 32 percent. A written quote for the reduced volume scenario was requested on 3 July 2024; as of the date of this approval record, it has not yet been received. 2.1 **Fill Rate:** PCS shall achieve a minimum fill rate of 90% for all confirmed staffing requests on a monthly rolling basis, calculated as the number of shifts filled divided by the number of shifts requested.

2.3 **Punctuality:** Assigned staff shall arrive at the Client's premises no later than 15 minutes prior to the scheduled shift start. PCS shall track arrival times and provide a monthly punctuality report to the Client.

2.4 **Skill Verification:** All staff provided shall have verifiable experience in the requested role. PCS shall maintain up-to-date records of each staff member's certifications, training, and prior assignments, and shall make such records available for Client audit upon reasonable notice.

2.5 **Substitution:** If a booked staff member is unable to attend, PCS shall provide a qualified substitute wherever possible. If no substitute is available, the Client shall be notified immediately and the shift shall be credited to the Client's account at the applicable rate.

4. DELIVERY SCHEDULES

4.1 The Buyer shall issue a rolling delivery schedule covering each calendar month, specifying the quantities, product mix, and delivery dates. Schedules shall be issued at least 10 working days before the first delivery date in the month.

4.2 Deliveries shall be made on the dates specified, between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday, excluding public holidays.

4.3 The Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing at least 48 hours before each delivery, confirming the vehicle registration, driver name, and estimated time of arrival.

4.4 Each delivery shall be accompanied by a delivery note stating the Goods, quantities, batch numbers, and the date of manufacture and expiry where applicable.

4.5 The Buyer shall provide reasonable access, unloading assistance, and storage space at the Delivery Point. Delays caused by the Buyer's failure to provide such facilities shall not constitute a breach by the Supplier, provided the Supplier's vehicle arrives within the agreed delivery window.

4.6 If the Supplier anticipates a delay of more than 4 hours, it shall inform the Buyer's procurement officer immediately and propose a revised delivery time. Repeated delays may be treated as a breach under Clause 11.

**3.1 Volume and Schedule**

Current weekly order: 25 tonnes (delivered in two drops: Tuesday and Friday).

There is a risk that if we need to revert to two drops later in the year (e.g., for the December festive season), the Friday slot may no longer be available. We will need to give Lagoon at least four weeks notice for any reversion.

With a single weekly delivery, the receiving team at the Festac store will need to process the full 15 tonnes in one day instead of splitting it across two days. The store manager has confirmed they can handle this with the current crew, but they will need the forklift operator to stay an extra hour on Tuesday. This has been budgeted for in the current staffing plan.

The Lekki store will continue to receive a transfer from Festac rather than a direct delivery. The transfer quantity will be reduced proportionally.

**3.4 Supplier Impact**

Lagoon Cold Chain has been informed verbally of the proposed reduction. Their account manager, Mrs. Adeyemi, noted that the 25-tonne weekly volume was a key factor in their pricing. Reducing to 15 tonnes may trigger a review of the unit price under Clause 8.2 of the framework agreement. **3.5 Quality Issues**

Change Request CR-2024-07 requested volume reduction in tons 10 tons. Record status: superseded.

1.3 The Agency shall use reasonable endeavours to fill all requests, but shall not be liable for failure to fill a request where the Client has not provided adequate notice or where the requested skill set is not reasonably available.

---

**2. SERVICE LEVELS**

2.1 **Fill Rate:** PCS shall achieve a minimum fill rate of 90% for all confirmed staffing requests on a monthly rolling basis, calculated as the number of shifts filled divided by the number of shifts requested.

2.2 **Response Time:** The Agency shall confirm availability of staff within 4 business hours of receiving a complete request. For emergency requests (less than 24 hours' notice), confirmation shall be provided within 2 hours.

2.3 **Punctuality:** Assigned staff shall arrive at the Client's premises no later than 15 minutes prior to the scheduled shift start. PCS shall track arrival times and provide a monthly punctuality report to the Client.

2.4 **Skill Verification:** All staff provided shall have verifiable experience in the requested role. PCS shall maintain up-to-date records of each staff member's certifications, training, and prior assignments, and shall make such records available for Client audit upon reasonable notice.

2.5 **Substitution:** If a booked staff member is unable to attend, PCS shall provide a qualified substitute wherever possible. If no substitute is available, the Client shall be notified immediately and the shift shall be credited to the Client's account at the applicable rate.

---

**3. STAFF AVAILABILITY AND NOTIFICATION**

3.1 PCS shall maintain a current register of available temporary staff. This register shall be updated daily and shall reflect the number of staff available for assignment on any given date.

3.2 Upon written request from the Client, PCS shall provide a written statement of the number of staff available for assignment. Such statement shall be deemed current as of the date stated therein.

3.3 **Current Availability (as of 15 November 2024):** Prime Catering Staffing lists available temp staff as of 2024-11-15 at 22. Record status: current. This figure is current and may be relied upon by the Client for planning purposes until the next daily update is issued.

3.4 The Agency shall notify the Client promptly of any material change to the available staff count, including any reduction of more than 20% from the most recently stated figure.

---

**4. RATE CARD AND BILLING**

4.1 The following rates shall apply for temporary staff assignments, quoted in Nigerian Naira (₦) per 8-hour shift:

4.2 Overtime shall be billed at 1.5 times the applicable shift rate, calculated pro-rata per hour. Overtime must be authorised in advance by the Client's designated manager.

4.3 A transportation allowance of ₦1,500 per shift shall be added to all assignments outside the Lagos Island area. For Abuja assignments, a transportation allowance of ₦2,000 per shift shall apply.

4.4 **Billing Cycle:** Invoices shall be issued weekly, on each Monday, covering all shifts completed in the preceding calendar week. Payment is due within 14 days of invoice date.

4.5 A late payment fee of 2% per month shall apply to any amount not paid by the due date.

4.6 All rates are exclusive of VAT, which shall be added at the prevailing statutory rate.

---

---

**6. BILLING PROCEDURES AND OVERTIME**

6.1 All invoices shall be issued electronically to the Client's designated billing contact. Each invoice shall itemise, per assignment:
   (a) the number of temporary staff supplied;
   (b) the number of shifts or hours worked;
   (c) the applicable rate per the rate card in Section 4;
   (d) any overtime, transportation, or other allowances;
   (e) VAT, if applicable.

6.2 Time sheets shall be submitted by PCS to the Client's designated manager on a daily basis. The Client's manager shall sign or otherwise approve each time sheet within 48 hours of receipt. Failure to dispute a time sheet within 48 hours shall be deemed acceptance of its contents.

6.3 Overtime rates shall be applied as follows:
   (a) Any hours worked beyond the standard 8-hour shift shall be billed at 1.5 times the applicable hourly rate, calculated pro-rata.
   (b) Work on public holidays shall be billed at 2.0 times the applicable hourly rate, unless otherwise agreed in writing in advance.
   (c) Night shifts, defined as any shift commencing after 22:00 and ending before 06:00, shall attract a night premium of 10% of the applicable shift rate.

6.4 For the avoidance of doubt, overtime shall only be payable where authorised in advance in writing by the Client's designated manager. Unauthorised overtime shall be the responsibility of the temporary staff member and shall not be billed to the Client.

6.5 Where a temporary staff member is required to work a split shift, the Client shall provide a rest period of not less than 2 hours between the two parts of the shift. No additional charge shall apply for the rest period, provided that the total working hours within the calendar day do not exceed 12 hours.

6.6 Billing disputes shall be raised in writing within 14 days of the invoice date. Any dispute shall be resolved within 7 business days of receipt. The undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid by the due date.

Prime Catering Staffing charges an hourly rate per temp staff in naira of 1800. Record status: current.

---

**7. RATE REVIEW AND ADJUSTMENT**

7.1 The rates set out in Section 4 shall remain in effect until 31 December 2024. Thereafter, PCS may review and adjust rates upon 30 days' written notice to the Client.

7.2 Any adjustment to rates shall be based on changes to the National Minimum Wage, inflation indices published by the National Bureau of Statistics, and prevailing market rates for temporary catering staff in Lagos and Abuja.

7.3 Where the Client requests a change to the scope of services, including changes to shift patterns, staffing levels, or the introduction of new service locations, PCS shall provide a revised quotation within 5 business days of the request. Such revised quotation shall be valid for 30 days.

7.4 The Client shall not be bound to accept any revised quotation, and may decline it in writing. In the event of such decline, the existing terms shall continue to apply to the original scope of services until the expiry of the notice period under Section 7.1.

---

**8. TERM AND TERMINATION**

8.1 This Agreement shall commence on 1 November 2024 and shall continue for an initial term of 12 months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Section 8.
